Al-Faqih Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn al-Qasim informed me, saying: Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Zayd al-'Adl related to us, saying: Abu Yahya al-Bazzaz related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Mansur related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Imran ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla related to us, saying: My father related to me, from Mujalid ibn 'Abd al-Wahid, from al-Hajjaj ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abu al-Khalil; and also from 'Ali ibn Zayd and 'Ata' ibn Abi Maymun, from Zayd ibn Habish, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the surah 'The Hour has drawn near' (iqtarabat al-sa'ah) every morning, will be raised on the Day of Resurrection with his face like the full moon on the night of the full moon. And whoever recites it every night, it is better, and he will come on the Day of Resurrection with his face radiant above the faces of all creation." [152] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 9/307.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿The Hour has drawn near﴾: the Resurrection has approached.

﴿And the moon has split﴾. Ibn Kaysan said: In the verse there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir); its meaning is: "The moon has split and the Hour has drawn near." What supports this is the reading of Hudhayfah: "The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has indeed split." 'Uthman ibn 'Ata' related from his father that its meaning is: "And the moon will split." But the scholars disagree with this, and the sound reports clearly state that this verse has already taken place.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Makki informed us, saying: Abu al-Azhar related to us, saying: Rawh related to us, from Shu'bah, who said: I heard Sulayman say: I heard Ibrahim narrate from Abu Ma'mar, from 'Abd Allah (ibn Mas'ud), that the moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) into two halves: one part was above the mountain and the other part below the mountain. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, bear witness." [153] [[Al-Sunan al-Kubra: 6/476, hadith 1155.]] He also said: "Bear witness." [154] [[Al-Sunan al-Kubra: 6/476, hadith 11553.]]

And Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Malik al-Qadi informed us, saying:

Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Sa'id related to us, saying: My father related to us, saying: Husayn related to us, from al-A'mash and 'Abdah al-Dabbi, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqamah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until I saw its two halves.

And 'Abd Allah informed us, saying: Makki informed us, saying: Abu al-Azhar related to us, saying: Rawh related to us, from Shu'bah, from Sulayman, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Umar, a report similar to the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud.

And 'Abd Allah informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Zayd al-Sayrafi informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn Harb related to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl related to us, saying: Husayn related to us, from Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from his father, who said: The moon split while we were with the Prophet (ﷺ) in Mecca.

And 'Abd Allah informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn al-Hasan al-Shaybani informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan related to us, saying: My father related to us, saying: Husayn related to us, from Sa'd, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas; and al-Hakam, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas; and Muqsim, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) into two parts: one part was at al-Suwaydla' and the other part at al-Jundamah.

'Aqil ibn Muhammad informed me that Abu al-Faraj al-Qadi narrated to them from Muhammad ibn Jarir, who said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Buza' related to me, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah related to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, that the people of Mecca asked the Prophet (ﷺ) to show them a sign, so he showed them the moon split into two halves, until they saw the mountain between them. [[Al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah: 6/85.]]

And with the same chain, from Muhammad ibn Jarir, who said: 'Ali ibn Sahl related to us, saying: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad related to us, from Shu'bah, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: The moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) twice.

And with the same chain, from Muhammad ibn Jarir, who said: Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib related to us, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, who said: We stopped at al-Mada'in, about a farsakh away from it. Then Friday came, and my father attended, and we attended with him. Hudhayfah delivered the sermon to us and said: "Behold, Allah, glory be to Him, says: ﴿The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split﴾. Behold, the Hour has indeed drawn near. Behold, the moon has indeed split. Behold, the world has announced its parting. Behold, today is the training ground and tomorrow is the race." I said to my father: "Will people race tomorrow?" He said: "My son, you are indeed ignorant. The race is only by deeds." Then the next Friday came, and we attended, and Hudhayfah delivered the sermon and said: "Behold, Allah says: ﴿The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split﴾. Behold, the Hour has drawn near. Behold, the moon has split. Behold, the world has announced its parting. Behold, today is the training ground, and tomorrow is the race. Behold, the goal is the Fire, and the one who wins is the one who reaches Paradise first."

And with the same chain from Ibn Jarir, who said: al-Hasan ibn Abi Yahya al-Maqdisi related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Abu 'Awanah related to us, from al-Mughirah, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from 'Abd Allah, who said: The moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Quraysh said: "This is the sorcery of Ibn Abi Kabshah; he has bewitched you." So they asked the travellers, and they asked them, and they said: "Yes, we have seen it." Then Allah, glory be to Him, revealed: ﴿The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split﴾.

﴿And if they see a sign, they turn away and say: "Continuous sorcery"﴾. Mustamirr means "passing away, about to vanish." It derives from their saying: marra al-shay' and istamarra, meaning it went away and vanished, and its counterpart is qarra and istaqarra. This is the view of Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Farra' and al-Kisa'i. Abu al-'Aliyah and al-Dahhak said: it means "firm, strong, powerful." Sufyan (al-Thawri) said, relating from Qatadah: "victorious." It derives from their saying: marra al-habl, when the rope became hard and strong, and amartuhu, when I twisted it tightly. Al-Rabi' said: "effective." Yaman said: "pressing on." Abu 'Ubaydah said: "false." It was also said: "some of it resembles other parts of it."

﴿And they denied and followed their desires, and every affair is settled﴾. He says: every affair, whether good or evil, has its settled place and its end. Good is settled for its people in Paradise, and evil is settled for its people in the Fire. Qatadah said: ﴿every affair is settled﴾: that is, for the people of good, good; and for the people of evil, evil. Muqatil said: every person has an end. It was also said: every affair has its reality. Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: it means the settling of their denial and the settling of the believers' affirmation, until they come to know its reality in reward and punishment. It was also said: its meaning is: whatever is decreed will certainly occur. It was said: for every one of My affairs that I have carried out in My creation, its settled place will not cease. Abu Hatim reported from Shaybah and Nafi' the reading mustaqirr with a fatha on the qaf, and al-Fadl ibn Shadhan reported from Abu Ja'far (reading) with a kasra on the ra'; but there is no basis for either of them.

Muqatil said: the moon split, then it became whole again after that.

﴿And there had certainly come to them﴾, meaning the people of Mecca, ﴿of the news that contained a deterrent (muzdajar)﴾, meaning a sufficient (mutanahi). Mujahid said this. Sufyan (said): "an end" (muntaha). It is a form of mufta'al from zajr (restraint), and its original form is muztajar, then the ta' was changed to dal.

﴿Far-reaching wisdom﴾, complete, without any deficiency, and it is the Qur'an. ﴿But warnings avail not﴾ when they deny and oppose them.

﴿So turn away from them﴾: it was abrogated by the verse of fighting (naskh). ﴿The day the caller calls to a thing unfamiliar (nukur)﴾: a dreadful, terrible, and great matter, which is the Fire. It was also said: it is the Resurrection. Al-Hasan and Ibn Kathir made the kaf light (nukur), while the others made it heavy (nukkur). Mujahid read (nukira), in the passive form, meaning "they consider it unknown."

﴿Humbled (khushha'an) their eyes﴾, meaning abased. It is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal); its meaning is: "They will come out of the graves humbled." Ibn 'Abbas, Ya'qub, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read (khashi'an) with an alif, in the singular, and Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred it, considering the reading of 'Abd Allah and Abu Raja': "their eyes humbled" (khashi'ah). The rest read (khushshan), without the alif, in the plural.

Al-Farra' and Abu 'Ubaydah said: when the nouns come after their verb, you have the choice between singular, plural, feminine and masculine. You may say: "I passed by men whose faces are beautiful" (husn wujuhuhum), "a woman whose faces are beautiful" (hasanah), and "men whose faces are beautiful" (hisan wujuhuhum). A poet said:

"And youths whose faces are handsome, from Iyad ibn Nizar ibn Ma'add."

Whoever uses the singular does so because it has the meaning of the plural; whoever uses the plural does so because they are descriptive adjectives, and adjectives are nouns; and whoever uses the feminine does so because the group is feminine. Another poet said:

"The riders throw them across the wide roads, with their necks stretched out, their camels driven forward with the reins at their ends."

Al-Farra' said: if he had said "mu'tarridah," "mu'tarridat," "muzjah," or "muzjiyat," all of that would have been permissible.

﴿They will come out of the graves (ajdath)﴾, the tombs, ﴿as if they were locusts scattered﴾, bewildered. He mentioned "scattered" according to the wording of "locusts," similar to ﴿like scattered moths﴾.

﴿Hastening (muhti'in) toward the caller﴾, hurrying, hastening, and turning eagerly. ﴿The disbelievers will say: "This is a difficult day."﴾

And 'Abd Allah informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn al-Hasan al-Shaybani informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan related to us, saying: My father related to us, saying: Husayn related to us, from Sa'd, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas; and al-Hakam, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas; and Muqsim, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) into two parts: one part was at al-Suwaydla' and the other part at al-Jundamah.

'Aqil ibn Muhammad informed me that Abu al-Faraj al-Qadi narrated to them from Muhammad ibn Jarir, who said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Buza' related to me, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah related to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, that the people of Mecca asked the Prophet (ﷺ) to show them a sign, so he showed them the moon split into two halves, until they saw the mountain between them. [[Al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah: 6/85.]]

And with the same chain, from Muhammad ibn Jarir, who said: 'Ali ibn Sahl related to us, saying: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad related to us, from Shu'bah, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: The moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) twice.

And with the same chain, from Muhammad ibn Jarir, who said: Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib related to us, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, who said: We stopped at al-Mada'in, about a farsakh away from it. Then Friday came, and my father attended, and we attended with him. Hudhayfah delivered the sermon to us and said: "Behold, Allah, glory be to Him, says: ﴿The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split﴾. Behold, the Hour has indeed drawn near. Behold, the moon has indeed split. Behold, the world has announced its parting. Behold, today is the training ground and tomorrow is the race." I said to my father: "Will people race tomorrow?" He said: "My son, you are indeed ignorant. The race is only by deeds." Then the next Friday came, and we attended, and Hudhayfah delivered the sermon and said: "Behold, Allah says: ﴿The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split﴾. Behold, the Hour has drawn near. Behold, the moon has split. Behold, the world has announced its parting. Behold, today is the training ground, and tomorrow is the race. Behold, the goal is the Fire, and the one who wins is the one who reaches Paradise first."

And with the same chain from Ibn Jarir, who said: al-Hasan ibn Abi Yahya al-Maqdisi related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Abu 'Awanah related to us, from al-Mughirah, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from 'Abd Allah, who said: The moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Quraysh said: "This is the sorcery of Ibn Abi Kabshah; he has bewitched you." So they asked the travellers, and they asked them, and they said: "Yes, we have seen it." Then Allah, glory be to Him, revealed: ﴿The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split﴾.

﴿And if they see a sign, they turn away and say: "Continuous sorcery"﴾. Mustamirr means "passing away, about to vanish." It derives from their saying: marra al-shay' and istamarra, meaning it went away and vanished, and its counterpart is qarra and istaqarra. This is the view of Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Farra' and al-Kisa'i. Abu al-'Aliyah and al-Dahhak said: it means "firm, strong, powerful." Sufyan (al-Thawri) said, relating from Qatadah: "victorious." It derives from their saying: marra al-habl, when the rope became hard and strong, and amartuhu, when I twisted it tightly. Al-Rabi' said: "effective." Yaman said: "pressing on." Abu 'Ubaydah said: "false." It was also said: "some of it resembles other parts of it."

﴿And they denied and followed their desires, and every affair is settled﴾. He says: every affair, whether good or evil, has its settled place and its end. Good is settled for its people in Paradise, and evil is settled for its people in the Fire. Qatadah said: ﴿every affair is settled﴾: that is, for the people of good, good; and for the people of evil, evil. Muqatil said: every person has an end. It was also said: every affair has its reality. Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: it means the settling of their denial and the settling of the believers' affirmation, until they come to know its reality in reward and punishment. It was also said: its meaning is: whatever is decreed will certainly occur. It was said: for every one of My affairs that I have carried out in My creation, its settled place will not cease. Abu Hatim reported from Shaybah and Nafi' the reading mustaqirr with a fatha on the qaf, and al-Fadl ibn Shadhan reported from Abu Ja'far (reading) with a kasra on the ra'; but there is no basis for either of them.

Muqatil said: the moon split, then it became whole again after that.

﴿And there had certainly come to them﴾, meaning the people of Mecca, ﴿of the news that contained a deterrent (muzdajar)﴾, meaning a sufficient (mutanahi). Mujahid said this. Sufyan (said): "an end" (muntaha). It is a form of mufta'al from zajr (restraint), and its original form is muztajar, then the ta' was changed to dal.

﴿Far-reaching wisdom﴾, complete, without any deficiency, and it is the Qur'an. ﴿But warnings avail not﴾ when they deny and oppose them.

﴿So turn away from them﴾: it was abrogated by the verse of fighting (naskh). ﴿The day the caller calls to a thing unfamiliar (nukur)﴾: a dreadful, terrible, and great matter, which is the Fire. It was also said: it is the Resurrection. Al-Hasan and Ibn Kathir made the kaf light (nukur), while the others made it heavy (nukkur). Mujahid read (nukira), in the passive form, meaning "they consider it unknown."

﴿Humbled (khushha'an) their eyes﴾, meaning abased. It is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal); its meaning is: "They will come out of the graves humbled." Ibn 'Abbas, Ya'qub, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read (khashi'an) with an alif, in the singular, and Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred it, considering the reading of 'Abd Allah and Abu Raja': "their eyes humbled" (khashi'ah). The rest read (khushshan), without the alif, in the plural.

Al-Farra' and Abu 'Ubaydah said: when the nouns come after their verb, you have the choice between singular, plural, feminine and masculine. You may say: "I passed by men whose faces are beautiful" (husn wujuhuhum), "a woman whose faces are beautiful" (hasanah), and "men whose faces are beautiful" (hisan wujuhuhum). A poet said:

"And youths whose faces are handsome, from Iyad ibn Nizar ibn Ma'add."

Whoever uses the singular does so because it has the meaning of the plural; whoever uses the plural does so because they are descriptive adjectives, and adjectives are nouns; and whoever uses the feminine does so because the group is feminine. Another poet said:

"The riders throw them across the wide roads, with their necks stretched out, their camels driven forward with the reins at their ends."

Al-Farra' said: if he had said "mu'tarridah," "mu'tarridat," "muzjah," or "muzjiyat," all of that would have been permissible.

﴿They will come out of the graves (ajdath)﴾, the tombs, ﴿as if they were locusts scattered﴾, bewildered. He mentioned "scattered" according to the wording of "locusts," similar to ﴿like scattered moths﴾.

﴿Hastening (muhti'in) toward the caller﴾, hurrying, hastening, and turning eagerly. ﴿The disbelievers will say: "This is a difficult day."﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 54, verse 9–21:

﴿Before them the people of Noah denied; they denied Our servant, and said, "He is a madman," and he was rebuked.﴾ That is, before the people of Makkah. "The people of Noah" denied His servant Noah, peace be upon him. "They said, 'He is a madman'" meaning: he is mad. "And he was rebuked" meaning: they rebuked him from his call and his message. Mujahid said: "istaṭara junūnan" (they claimed he was mad). Ibn Zayd said: they accused him, rebuked him, and threatened him. ﴿"If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be among those stoned."﴾

﴿So he called upon his Lord: "I am overpowered, so help me (fa-intaṣir)"﴾ meaning: overcome, subdued. "Then avenge me on them."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: al-Rawandi narrated to us, saying: Yusuf ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from Abd ibn Umayr, who said: "A man from the people of Noah would meet him, and would choke him until he fell unconscious. When he regained consciousness he would say: 'My Lord, forgive my people, for they do not know.'"

﴿So We opened the gates of heaven with water pouring forth﴾ pouring out, gushing; it did not cease or stop for forty days.

Ibn Abbas and al-Qurazi said: "gushing forth from the earth." Yaman said: a layer between heaven and earth. Abu Ubayda said: "hayil" (pouring). al-Kisa'i said: "sa'il" (flowing). Imru' al-Qays said, describing rain:

"The breeze stirred it, then it turned, and in it was a southern downpour, pouring forth."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/132.]]

And Salama ibn Jandal said, describing a horse:

"The water pouring, the running rushing down, the reeds pressed, and the color a deep black."
[[al-Sihah: 1/202.]]

﴿And We caused the earth to burst forth with springs﴾ meaning: We split the earth with water, ﴿so the waters met﴾ meaning the water of the sky and the water of the earth. He said "the water met," though meeting does not occur from one but from two or more, because "al-ma'" (water) is both collective and singular.

ʿĀṣim al-Jahdari read "fa-iltaqa al-mā'ān" (the two waters met), and al-Hasan read "fa-iltaqa al-māwān," making one of the two alifs a waw.

﴿For a matter already decreed﴾ — it had been decided against them in the Mother of the Book.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: "Sustenance existed before bodies, and the decree existed before the trial," and he recited this verse.

﴿And We carried him upon a vessel of planks and nails﴾ — he mentioned the attribute and omitted the noun; its meaning: upon a ship of wooden planks and nails (dusur). Its singular is dissar. It is said from it: "dasartu al-safina" (I fastened the ship) when one fastens it with nails. This is the saying of al-Qurazi, Qatada, Ibn Zayd, the narration of al-Walibi from Ibn Abbas, and Shahr ibn Hawshab: it is the prow of the ship, named so because it thrusts the water with its breast, i.e., pushes. This is also the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn Abbas, who said: "al-dusur: the chest of the ship." The origin of dasr is dragging and pushing, and from it is the hadith concerning ambergris: "It is only something the sea has cast up" — i.e., pushed out and thrown up. Mujahid said: they are the ribs of the ship. al-Dahhak: the planks of its sides, and the dusur its base and its ends. Layth ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid: its ribs.

﴿Running before Our eyes﴾ — meaning: within Our sight. Muqatil ibn Hayyan: "by Our protection," and from it the people's saying to tears: "May God's eye be upon you." Muqatil ibn Sulayman: "by Our revelation." Sufyan: "by Our command."

﴿A recompense for him who had been disbelieved﴾ — meaning: We did that as a reward for Noah. The sense of the verse: for whoever denied and rejected and disbelieved in God. Some scholars took "man" here to mean "ma," saying its meaning is: a recompense for what was disbelieved of God's favours and blessings by those whom He drowned; this was the view of Ibn Zayd. It was also said: its meaning is that We punished them for God and because of their disbelief in Him.

Mujahid read "jaza'an li-man kāna kafara" with a fatḥa on the kaf and fa', meaning: the drowning was a recompense for one who disbelieves in God and denies His messenger, so God destroyed them.

None of the disbelievers escaped drowning except ʿŪj ibn ʿUnq, for the water reached only to his waist. The reason for his deliverance, as mentioned, was that Noah, peace be upon him, needed teak wood for the ship, but could not transport it, so ʿŪj carried that log to him from al-Sham. God, the Exalted, thanked him for that and saved him from drowning.

﴿And We left it﴾ — meaning the ship — ﴿as a sign﴾, a lesson.

Qatada said: God preserved it at Baqardā in the land of al-Jazira as a lesson and a sign, until the early generations of this community looked upon it, and how many ships came after it that had become ruins.

﴿So is there anyone who will take heed?﴾ — one who is admonished, who takes lesson, and who fears a punishment like theirs.

﴿So how was My punishment and My warning?﴾ — that is, My admonition. al-Farra' said: "al-inḏār" and "al-nudhur" are both verbal nouns; the Arabs say: "anzartu inḏāran wa-nudhran," as you say: "anfaqtu infāqan wa-nafaqatan," and "ayqantu iyqānan wa-yaqīnan."

﴿And We have made the Qur'an easy for remembrance﴾ — meaning: We facilitated and made it easy so that one may remember, take lesson, and reflect upon it. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "We made it easy for memorization outwardly, and there is no book of God's books that is read entirely by heart except the Qur'an." ﴿So is there anyone who will take heed?﴾ — admonished by its exhortations.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Rahawayh narrated to us, saying: Abu Umayr ibn al-Nahhas narrated to us in Bayt al-Maqdis, saying: Damra ibn Rabi'a narrated to us from Abdullah ibn Shawdhab from Mutar al-Warraq, concerning God's word ﴿So is there anyone who will take heed?﴾, he said: "Is there anyone seeking knowledge who will be helped in it?"

﴿Ad denied, so how was My punishment and My warning? Indeed, We sent upon them a furious wind on a day of ill omen, continuous misfortune﴾ — it was a Wednesday; "mustamirr" means severe, persisting, passing over the small and the great, so it left none of them without destroying him. Harun al-A'war read "naḥsin" with a kasra on the ha'.

﴿Uprooting people as though they were trunks of uprooted palm trees﴾ — it uproots people, then throws them on their heads so their necks break. Ibn Ishaq said: When the wind rose, seven men of 'Ad stood up — six of them, as is named to us, from the strongest and largest of 'Ad: Amr ibn al-Hilli, al-Harith ibn Shaddad, al-Halqam, the two sons of Tayqan, and Khaljan ibn Sa'd — and they put the women and children into a ravine between two mountains, then lined up at the mouth of the ravine to ward off the wind from those inside. But the wind began to strike them one by one. A woman of 'Ad said:

"Time has taken Amr ibn Hilli, and al-Hunayyat,
then al-Harith and al-Halqam, who climbed the passes.
And he who blocked the path of the wind in the days of calamity."
[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 27/130, where it reads: "sadda 'alayna al-rih".]]

And with the chain of Abu Hamza al-Thumali: he said: Muhammad ibn Sufyan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Qurza ibn Ka'b, from his father, from the Messenger of God ﷺ, who said: "The wind uprooted people from their graves."
[155] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/136.]]

﴿As though they were trunks of uprooted palm trees﴾ — Ibn Abbas said: "usul" (roots). al-Dahhak said: "awrak" (thighs). ﴿of uprooted palm trees﴾ — uprooted from its place, fallen upon the ground. The singular of a'jaz is ajz, like 'adud and a'dad. He said "a'jaz nakhl" (trunks of palm trees) although they were roots whose branches had been cut, because the wind was throwing their heads from their bodies, so bodies remained without heads.

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Junayni say: I heard Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Qadi al-Bayhaqi say: I heard Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Qasim ibn Sayyab al-Anbari say: al-Mubarrad was asked in the presence of Isma'il ibn Ishaq al-Qadi about a thousand questions, and among them was this: the questioner said: What is the difference between His saying "jā'athā rīḥun 'āṣif" and "li-Sulayman al-rīḥ 'āṣifatan," and His saying "ka-annahum a'jaz nakhlin khāwiyatin" and "ka-annahum a'jaz nakhlin munqa'ir"? He replied: Whatever comes to you from this category, you may refer it to the wording for the masculine, and you may refer it to the meaning for the feminine.

﴿So how was My punishment and My warning?﴾

Mujahid said: "istaṭara junūnan" (they claimed he was mad). Ibn Zayd said: they accused him, rebuked him, and threatened him. ﴿"If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be among those stoned."﴾

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: al-Rawandi narrated to us, saying: Yusuf ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from Abd ibn Umayr, who said: "A man from the people of Noah would meet him, and would choke him until he fell unconscious. When he regained consciousness he would say: 'My Lord, forgive my people, for they do not know.'"

﴿So We opened the gates of heaven with water pouring forth﴾ pouring out, gushing; it did not cease or stop for forty days.

Ibn Abbas and al-Qurazi said: "gushing forth from the earth." Yaman said: a layer between heaven and earth. Abu Ubayda said: "hayil" (pouring). al-Kisa'i said: "sa'il" (flowing). Imru' al-Qays said, describing rain:

"The breeze stirred it, then it turned, and in it was a southern downpour, pouring forth."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/132.]]

And Salama ibn Jandal said, describing a horse:

"The water pouring, the running rushing down, the reeds pressed, and the color a deep black."
[[al-Sihah: 1/202.]]

﴿And We caused the earth to burst forth with springs﴾ meaning: We split the earth with water, ﴿so the waters met﴾ meaning the water of the sky and the water of the earth. He said "the water met," though meeting does not occur from one but from two or more, because "al-ma'" (water) is both collective and singular.

ʿĀṣim al-Jahdari read "fa-iltaqa al-mā'ān" (the two waters met), and al-Hasan read "fa-iltaqa al-māwān," making one of the two alifs a waw.

﴿For a matter already decreed﴾ — it had been decided against them in the Mother of the Book.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: "Sustenance existed before bodies, and the decree existed before the trial," and he recited this verse.

﴿And We carried him upon a vessel of planks and nails﴾ — he mentioned the attribute and omitted the noun; its meaning: upon a ship of wooden planks and nails (dusur). Its singular is dissar. It is said from it: "dasartu al-safina" (I fastened the ship) when one fastens it with nails. This is the saying of al-Qurazi, Qatada, Ibn Zayd, the narration of al-Walibi from Ibn Abbas, and Shahr ibn Hawshab: it is the prow of the ship, named so because it thrusts the water with its breast, i.e., pushes. This is also the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn Abbas, who said: "al-dusur: the chest of the ship." The origin of dasr is dragging and pushing, and from it is the hadith concerning ambergris: "It is only something the sea has cast up" — i.e., pushed out and thrown up. Mujahid said: they are the ribs of the ship. al-Dahhak: the planks of its sides, and the dusur its base and its ends. Layth ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid: its ribs.

﴿Running before Our eyes﴾ — meaning: within Our sight. Muqatil ibn Hayyan: "by Our protection," and from it the people's saying to tears: "May God's eye be upon you." Muqatil ibn Sulayman: "by Our revelation." Sufyan: "by Our command."

﴿A recompense for him who had been disbelieved﴾ — meaning: We did that as a reward for Noah. The sense of the verse: for whoever denied and rejected and disbelieved in God. Some scholars took "man" here to mean "ma," saying its meaning is: a recompense for what was disbelieved of God's favours and blessings by those whom He drowned; this was the view of Ibn Zayd. It was also said: its meaning is that We punished them for God and because of their disbelief in Him.

Mujahid read "jaza'an li-man kāna kafara" with a fatḥa on the kaf and fa', meaning: the drowning was a recompense for one who disbelieves in God and denies His messenger, so God destroyed them.

None of the disbelievers escaped drowning except ʿŪj ibn ʿUnq, for the water reached only to his waist. The reason for his deliverance, as mentioned, was that Noah, peace be upon him, needed teak wood for the ship, but could not transport it, so ʿŪj carried that log to him from al-Sham. God, the Exalted, thanked him for that and saved him from drowning.

﴿And We left it﴾ — meaning the ship — ﴿as a sign﴾, a lesson.

Qatada said: God preserved it at Baqardā in the land of al-Jazira as a lesson and a sign, until the early generations of this community looked upon it, and how many ships came after it that had become ruins.

﴿So how was My punishment and My warning?﴾ — that is, My admonition. al-Farra' said: "al-inḏār" and "al-nudhur" are both verbal nouns; the Arabs say: "anzartu inḏāran wa-nudhran," as you say: "anfaqtu infāqan wa-nafaqatan," and "ayqantu iyqānan wa-yaqīnan."

﴿Ad denied, so how was My punishment and My warning? Indeed, We sent upon them a furious wind on a day of ill omen, continuous misfortune﴾ — it was a Wednesday; "mustamirr" means severe, persisting, passing over the small and the great, so it left none of them without destroying him. Harun al-A'war read "naḥsin" with a kasra on the ha'.

﴿Uprooting people as though they were trunks of uprooted palm trees﴾ — it uproots people, then throws them on their heads so their necks break. "Time has taken Amr ibn Hilli, and al-Hunayyat,
then al-Harith and al-Halqam, who climbed the passes.
And he who blocked the path of the wind in the days of calamity."
[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 27/130, where it reads: "sadda 'alayna al-rih".]]

He said "a'jaz nakhl" (trunks of palm trees) although they were roots whose branches had been cut, because the wind was throwing their heads from their bodies, so bodies remained without heads.

He replied: Whatever comes to you from this category, you may refer it to the wording for the masculine, and you may refer it to the meaning for the feminine.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: al-Rawandi narrated to us, saying: Yusuf ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from Abd ibn Umayr, who said: "A man from the people of Noah would meet him, and would choke him until he fell unconscious. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/132.]]

[[al-Sihah: 1/202.]]

This is also the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn Abbas, who said: "al-dusur: the chest of the ship." The origin of dasr is dragging and pushing, and from it is the hadith concerning ambergris: "It is only something the sea has cast up" — i.e., pushed out and thrown up. Mujahid said: they are the ribs of the ship. al-Dahhak: the planks of its sides, and the dusur its base and its ends. Layth ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid: its ribs.

﴿Running before Our eyes﴾ — meaning: within Our sight. Muqatil ibn Hayyan: "by Our protection," and from it the people's saying to tears: "May God's eye be upon you." Muqatil ibn Sulayman: "by Our revelation." Sufyan: "by Our command."

Some scholars took "man" here to mean "ma," saying its meaning is: a recompense for what was disbelieved of God's favours and blessings by those whom He drowned; this was the view of Ibn Zayd. It was also said: its meaning is that We punished them for God and because of their disbelief in Him.

Mujahid read "jaza'an li-man kāna kafara" with a fatḥa on the kaf and fa', meaning: the drowning was a recompense for one who disbelieves in God and denies His messenger, so God destroyed them.

None of the disbelievers escaped drowning except ʿŪj ibn ʿUnq, for the water reached only to his waist. The reason for his deliverance, as mentioned, was that Noah, peace be upon him, needed teak wood for the ship, but could not transport it, so ʿŪj carried that log to him from al-Sham. ﴿Ad denied, so how was My punishment and My warning? Indeed, We sent upon them a furious wind on a day of ill omen, continuous misfortune﴾ — it was a Wednesday; "mustamirr" means severe, persisting, passing over the small and the great, so it left none of them without destroying him. Indeed, We sent upon them a furious wind on a day of ill omen, continuous misfortune﴾ — it was a Wednesday; "mustamirr" means severe, persisting, passing over the small and the great, so it left none of them without destroying him. "Time has taken Amr ibn Hilli, and al-Hunayyat,
then al-Harith and al-Halqam, who climbed the passes.

﴿So how was My punishment and My warning?﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 54, verse 9–21:

﴿Before them the people of Noah denied; they denied Our servant, and said, "He is a madman," and he was rebuked.﴾ That is, before the people of Makkah. "The people of Noah" denied His servant Noah, peace be upon him. "They said, 'He is a madman'" meaning: he is mad. "And he was rebuked" meaning: they rebuked him from his call and his message. Mujahid said: "istaṭara junūnan" (they claimed he was mad). Ibn Zayd said: they accused him, rebuked him, and threatened him. ﴿"If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be among those stoned."﴾

﴿So he called upon his Lord: "I am overpowered, so help me (fa-intaṣir)"﴾ meaning: overcome, subdued. "Then avenge me on them."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: al-Rawandi narrated to us, saying: Yusuf ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from Abd ibn Umayr, who said: "A man from the people of Noah would meet him, and would choke him until he fell unconscious. When he regained consciousness he would say: 'My Lord, forgive my people, for they do not know.'"

﴿So We opened the gates of heaven with water pouring forth﴾ pouring out, gushing; it did not cease or stop for forty days.

Ibn Abbas and al-Qurazi said: "gushing forth from the earth." Yaman said: a layer between heaven and earth. Abu Ubayda said: "hayil" (pouring). al-Kisa'i said: "sa'il" (flowing). Imru' al-Qays said, describing rain:

"The breeze stirred it, then it turned, and in it was a southern downpour, pouring forth."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/132.]]

And Salama ibn Jandal said, describing a horse:

"The water pouring, the running rushing down, the reeds pressed, and the color a deep black."
[[al-Sihah: 1/202.]]

﴿And We caused the earth to burst forth with springs﴾ meaning: We split the earth with water, ﴿so the waters met﴾ meaning the water of the sky and the water of the earth. He said "the water met," though meeting does not occur from one but from two or more, because "al-ma'" (water) is both collective and singular.

ʿĀṣim al-Jahdari read "fa-iltaqa al-mā'ān" (the two waters met), and al-Hasan read "fa-iltaqa al-māwān," making one of the two alifs a waw.

﴿For a matter already decreed﴾ — it had been decided against them in the Mother of the Book.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: "Sustenance existed before bodies, and the decree existed before the trial," and he recited this verse.

﴿And We carried him upon a vessel of planks and nails﴾ — he mentioned the attribute and omitted the noun; its meaning: upon a ship of wooden planks and nails (dusur). Its singular is dissar. It is said from it: "dasartu al-safina" (I fastened the ship) when one fastens it with nails. This is the saying of al-Qurazi, Qatada, Ibn Zayd, the narration of al-Walibi from Ibn Abbas, and Shahr ibn Hawshab: it is the prow of the ship, named so because it thrusts the water with its breast, i.e., pushes. This is also the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn Abbas, who said: "al-dusur: the chest of the ship." The origin of dasr is dragging and pushing, and from it is the hadith concerning ambergris: "It is only something the sea has cast up" — i.e., pushed out and thrown up. Mujahid said: they are the ribs of the ship. al-Dahhak: the planks of its sides, and the dusur its base and its ends. Layth ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid: its ribs.

﴿Running before Our eyes﴾ — meaning: within Our sight. Muqatil ibn Hayyan: "by Our protection," and from it the people's saying to tears: "May God's eye be upon you." Muqatil ibn Sulayman: "by Our revelation." Sufyan: "by Our command."

﴿A recompense for him who had been disbelieved﴾ — meaning: We did that as a reward for Noah. The sense of the verse: for whoever denied and rejected and disbelieved in God. Some scholars took "man" here to mean "ma," saying its meaning is: a recompense for what was disbelieved of God's favours and blessings by those whom He drowned; this was the view of Ibn Zayd. It was also said: its meaning is that We punished them for God and because of their disbelief in Him.

Mujahid read "jaza'an li-man kāna kafara" with a fatḥa on the kaf and fa', meaning: the drowning was a recompense for one who disbelieves in God and denies His messenger, so God destroyed them.

None of the disbelievers escaped drowning except ʿŪj ibn ʿUnq, for the water reached only to his waist. The reason for his deliverance, as mentioned, was that Noah, peace be upon him, needed teak wood for the ship, but could not transport it, so ʿŪj carried that log to him from al-Sham. God, the Exalted, thanked him for that and saved him from drowning.

﴿And We left it﴾ — meaning the ship — ﴿as a sign﴾, a lesson.

Qatada said: God preserved it at Baqardā in the land of al-Jazira as a lesson and a sign, until the early generations of this community looked upon it, and how many ships came after it that had become ruins.

﴿وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا الْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِنْ مُدَّكِرٍ﴾ ﴿كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِالنُّذُرِ﴾ ﴿فَقالُوا أَبَشَراً مِنَّا وَاحِداً نَتَّبِعُهُ إِنَّا إِذاً لَفِي ضَلالٍ وَسُعُرٍ﴾. "أبشراً آدميّا واحدا منّا نتبعه ونحن جماعة كثيرة وهو واحد": وقرأ أبو السماك العدوي بالرفع، وكلا الوجهين سائغ في عائد الذكر. ﴿إِنَّا إِذاً﴾: إن فعلنا ذلك وتركنا دين آبائنا وتابعناه على دينه، وهو واحد منا آدمي مثلنا. ﴿لَفِي ضَلالٍ﴾: ذهاب عن الصواب. ﴿وَسُعُرٍ﴾: قال ابن عباس: يعني وعذاب. وقال الحسن: شدة العذاب. وقال قتادة: عناء. وقال سفيان بن عيينة: هو جمع سعيرة. وقال الفراء: جنون، يقال: ناقة مسعورة إذا كانت خفيفة الرأس هائمة على وجهها. قال الشاعر يصف ناقة:

تخال بها سعرا إذا السفر هزها ... ذميل وإيقاع من السير متعب [تفسير القرطبي: 17/138.]

وقال وهب: ﴿وَسُعُرٍ﴾: أي بُعد من الحق.

﴿أَأُلْقِيَ الذِّكْرُ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ بَيْنِنَا﴾: أأُنزل الوحي عليه من بيننا؟ ﴿بَلْ هُوَ كَذَّابٌ أَشِرٌ﴾: بطِر، مرِح، متكبر، يريد أن يتعاظم علينا بادعائه النبوة.

وقال عبد الرحمن بن أبي حماد: الأشِر هو الذي لا يبالي ما قال. وقرأ مجاهد ﴿أَشُرٌ﴾ بفتح الألف وضم الشين، وهما لغتان مثل: حَذِر وحَذُر، ويَقِظ ويَقُظ، وعَجِل وعَجُل، ومَجِد ومَجُد الشجاع.

﴿سَيَعْلَمُونَ غَداً﴾: بالتاء قراءة الشامي، وقرأ الأعمش ويحيى وابن ثوبان وحمزة وغيرهم بالياء. فمن قرأ بالتاء فهو من قول صالح لهم، ومن قرأ بالياء فهو من قول الله سبحانه. ومعنى الكلام: في الغد القريب، على عادة الناس في قولهم للعواقب: إنّ مع اليوم غداً، وإنّ مع اليوم أخاه غداً، وأراد به وقت نزول العذاب بهم. ﴿مَنِ الْكَذَّابُ الْأَشِرُ﴾: قرأ أبو قلابة ﴿مَنِ الْكَذَّابُ الْأَشَرُّ﴾ بفتح الشين وتشديد الراء على وزن أفعل من الشر، والقراءة الصحيحة ما عليه العامة.

قال أبو حاتم: لا يكاد العربي يتكلم بالأشرّ والأخيّر إلا في ضرورة الشعر، كقول رؤبة:

بلال خير الناس وابن الأخير

إنما يقولون: خير وشر. قال الله عز وجل: ﴿كُنْتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ﴾، وقال سبحانه: ﴿أَنْتُمْ شَرٌّ مَكاناً﴾.

﴿إِنَّا مُرْسِلُوا النَّاقَةِ﴾: باعثوها ومخرجوها من الهضبة التي سألوا. ﴿فِتْنَةً لَهُمْ﴾: محنة. ﴿فَارْتَقِبْهُمْ﴾: وانتظرهم، ﴿وَاصْطَبِرْ﴾: واصبر على ظلمهم وأذاهم، ولا تعجل حتى يأتيهم أمري. ﴿وَاصْطَبِرْ﴾ افتعال من الصبر، وأصل الطاء فيه تاء، فحُوِّلت طاءً لأجل الصاد.

﴿وَنَبِّئْهُمْ أَنَّ الْمَاءَ قِسْمَةٌ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ وبين الناقة بالسوية: لها يوم ولهم يوم. وإنما قال: ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ لأن العرب إذا أخبرت عن بني آدم وعن البهائم غلّبوا بني آدم على البهائم. ﴿كُلُّ شِرْبٍ مُحْتَضَرٌ﴾: نصيب من الماء يحضره من كانت نوبته، فإذا كان يوم الناقة حضرت شربها، وإذا كان يومهم حضروا شربهم. وقال مجاهد: يعني يحضرون الماء إذا غابت الناقة، وإذا جاءت حضروا اللبن.

﴿فَنَادَوْا صاحِبَهُمْ فَتَعاطى فَعَقَرَ﴾: صاحبهم هو قدار بن سالف، وكان أشقر، ولذلك قيل له: أشقر ثمود. فتناول الناقة بسيفه فعقرها، ولذلك سمّت العرب الجزار "قداراً" تشبيهاً به. وقال الشاعر:

إنا لنضرب بالسيوف رؤوسهم ... ضرب القدار نقيعة القدام [تفسير القرطبي: 17/139.]

﴿فَكَيْفَ كانَ عَذابِي وَنُذُرِ﴾. ثم بيّن عذابهم فقال عز من قائل: ﴿إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ صَيْحَةً واحِدَةً فَكانُوا كَهَشِيمِ الْمُحْتَظِرِ﴾. قرأ الحسن وقتادة ﴿الْمُحْتَظَرِ﴾ بفتح الظاء، أراد الحظيرة، وقرأ الباقون بكسر الظاء، أرادوا صاحب الحظيرة.

قال ابن عباس: هو أن الرجل يجعل لغنمه حظيرة بالشجر والشوك دون السباع، فما سقط من ذلك فداسته الغنم فهو الهشيم. وقال قتادة: يعني كالعظام النخرة المحترقة، وهي رواية العوفي عن ابن عباس، ورواية أبي ظبيان عنه أيضاً. وقيل: كحشيش تأكله الغنم. وقال سعيد بن جبير: هو التراب الذي يتناثر من الحائط. وقال ابن زيد: هو الشجر البالي الذي تهشّم حتى ذرّته الريح، والعرب تسمي كل شيء كان رطباً فيبس هشيماً.

﴿وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا﴾ هوّنّا عليهم ﴿الْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِنْ مُدَّكِرٍ﴾. ﴿كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ لُوطٍ بِالنُّذُرِ﴾. ﴿إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ حاصِباً﴾: ريحاً ترميهم بالحَصْباء، وهي الحصى. وقال بعضهم: هو الحجر نفسه. قال الضحاك: يعني صغار الحصى. والحاصب والحَصْب والحَصْباء هي الحجر الذي دون ملء الكف، والمحصَّب الموضع الذي يُرمى فيه الجمار. وقال سعيد بن المسيب: سمعت عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه يقول لأهل المدينة: "حصّبوا المسجد"، أي صبّوا فيه الحجارة.

﴿ثم استثنى فقال: إِلَّا آلَ لُوطٍ﴾: أي أتباعه على دينه من أهله وأمته، ﴿نَجَّيْناهُمْ﴾ من العذاب ﴿بِسَحَرٍ﴾. قال الأخفش: إنما أجراه لأنه نكرة، ومجازه: بسحرٍ من الأسحار، ولو أراد سحر يوم بعينه لقال: "سَحَرَ" غير مجرى، ونظيره قوله: ﴿اهْبِطُوا مِصْراً﴾.

﴿نِعْمَةً﴾ يعني: كان ذلك، أو جعلناه ﴿نِعْمَةً مِنْ عِنْدِنا﴾ عليهم حيث أنجيناهم وأهلكنا أعداءهم. ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾ كما جزيناهم، لوطاً وآله، ﴿نَجْزِي مَنْ شَكَرَ﴾ فآمن بالله وأطاعه.

﴿وَلَقَدْ أَنْذَرَهُمْ لوط بَطْشَتَنا﴾ أي أخذنا لهم بالعقوبة قبل حلولها بهم. ﴿فَتَمارَوْا بِالنُّذُرِ﴾ فكذّبوا بإنذاره شكاً منهم فيه، وهو تفاعل من المِرية.

﴿وَلَقَدْ راوَدُوهُ عَنْ ضَيْفِهِ﴾: طالبوه وسألوه أن يُخلّي بينهم وبينهم. يقول العرب: راده يرُوده، وارتاده، وراوده يراوده، نظيرها. ﴿وَراوَدَتْهُ الَّتِي هُوَ فِي بَيْتِها عَنْ نَفْسِهِ﴾.

﴿فَطَمَسْنا أَعْيُنَهُمْ﴾ أي أعميناهم، وصيّرناها كسائر الوجه لا يُرى لها شق. وذلك أنهم لما قصدوا دار لوط عليه السلام وعالجوا بابه ليدخلوا، قالت الرسل للوط: خلِّ بينهم وبين الدخول، ﴿فَإِنَّا رُسُلُ رَبِّكَ لَنْ يَصِلُوا إِلَيْكَ﴾. فدخلوا الدار، فاستأذن جبريل ربَّه عز وجل في عقوبتهم فأذن له، فصفقهم بجناحه، فتركهم عمياً يترددون متحيرين لا يهتدون إلى الباب، وأخرجهم لوط عمياً لا يبصرون. هذا قول عامة المفسرين. وقال الضحاك: طمس الله على أبصارهم، فلم يروا الرسل، وقالوا: قد رأيناهم حين دخلوا البيت، فأين ذهبوا؟ فلم يروهم، ورجعوا. ﴿فَذُوقُوا عَذابِي وَنُذُرِ﴾.

﴿وَلَقَدْ صَبَّحَهُمْ﴾ جاءهم العذاب وقت الصبح ﴿بُكْرَةً عَذابٌ مُسْتَقِرٌّ﴾ دائم عام، استقر فيهم حتى يُقضى بهم إلى عذاب الآخرة.

﴿فَذُوقُوا عَذابِي وَنُذُرِ﴾. ﴿وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا الْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِنْ مُدَّكِرٍ﴾. ﴿وَلَقَدْ جاءَ آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ النُّذُرُ﴾ يعني موسى وهارون عليهما السلام. ﴿كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا التسع كُلِّها فَأَخَذْناهُمْ بالعذاب أَخْذَ عَزِيزٍ مُقْتَدِرٍ﴾: قادر لا يعجزه ما أراد.

ثم خوّف أهل مكة فقال عز من قائل: ﴿أَكُفَّارُكُمْ خَيْرٌ مِنْ أُولئِكُمْ﴾ الذين أحللت بهم نقمتي: من قوم نوح، وعاد، وثمود، وقوم لوط، وآل فرعون؟ ﴿أَمْ لَكُمْ بَراءَةٌ﴾ من العذاب ﴿فِي الزُّبُرِ﴾: الكتب، تأمنون بها؟

﴿أَمْ يَقُولُونَ﴾ يعني كفار مكة: ﴿نَحْنُ جَمِيعٌ مُنْتَصِرٌ﴾ أي جماعة لا تُرام ولا تُضام، ولا يقصدنا أحد بسوء، ولا يريد حربنا وتفريق جمعنا إلا انتقمنا منه. وكان حقه: "منتصرون"، فتبع رؤوس الآي.

﴿سَيُهْزَمُ الْجَمْعُ﴾: قراءة العامة على غير تسمية الفاعل، وقرأ يعقوب بالنون والنصب وكسر الزاي وفتح العين على التعظيم. ﴿وَيُوَلُّونَ الدُّبُرَ﴾ أي الأدبار، فوحّد والمراد الجمع لأجل رؤوس الآي، كما يقال: ضربنا منهم الرؤوس، وضربنا منهم الرأس، إذا كان الواحد يؤدي عن معنى جميعه. فصدق الله سبحانه وتعالى وعده، وهزمهم يوم بدر.

قال مقاتل: ضرب أبو جهل فرسه فتقدم يوم بدر في الصف وقال: "نحن منتصرون اليوم من محمد وأصحابه".

قال سعيد بن المسيب: سمعت عمر بن الخطاب لما نزلت ﴿سَيُهْزَمُ الْجَمْعُ وَيُوَلُّونَ الدُّبُرَ﴾ قال: كنت لا أدري أي جمع نُهزم؟ فلما كان يوم بدر رأيت النبي ﷺ ثبت في درعه ويقول: ﴿سَيُهْزَمُ الْجَمْعُ وَيُوَلُّونَ الدُّبُرَ﴾.

﴿بَلِ السَّاعَةُ مَوْعِدُهُمْ﴾ جميعاً، ﴿وَالسَّاعَةُ أَدْهى وَأَمَرُّ﴾: أعظم بليّةً وأشد مرارةً من عذاب يوم بدر.

أخبرني الحسين بن محمد قال: حدّثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: حدّثنا محمد بن إبراهيم بن زياد قال: حدّثنا أبو مصعب قال: حدّثنا مجرد بن هارون، عن الأعرج، عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: «بادروا بالأعمال سبعاً: ما ينتظرون إلا فقراً منسياً، أو غنىً مطغياً [الصحاح: 3/1293.]، أو مرضاً مفسداً، أو هرماً مفنداً، أو موتاً مجهزاً، والدجال شر غائب يُنتظر، والساعة أدهى وأمر».

[156]

﴿إِنَّ الْمُجْرِمِينَ فِي ضَلالٍ وَسُعُرٍ﴾: قال الضحاك: يعني ناراً ستُعرض عليهم.

قال الحسين بن الفضل: ﴿إِنَّ الْمُجْرِمِينَ فِي ضَلالٍ﴾ في الدنيا، ﴿وَسُعُرٍ﴾ نارٍ في الآخرة. وقال ابن كيسان: بُعدٍ من الحق. وقيل: جنون. وقال قتادة: في عناء وعذاب. ثم بيّن عذابهم فقال: ﴿يَوْمَ يُسْحَبُونَ فِي النَّارِ عَلى وُجُوهِهِمْ﴾ يُجرّون، ويقال لهم: ﴿ذُوقُوا مَسَّ سَقَرَ﴾، وإنما هو كقولك: "ذق المرَّ، السياطَ".

﴿إِنَّا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ﴾ بالنصب قراءة العامة، وقرأ أبو السماك العدوي بالرفع ﴿خَلَقْناهُ بِقَدَرٍ﴾. قال الحسن: قدّر الله لكل شيء من خلقه قدرَه الذي ينبغي له. وقال الربيع: هو كقوله: ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدْراً﴾، أي أجلاً لا يتقدم ولا يتأخر. وقال ابن عباس: ﴿إِنَّا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ جَعَلْنا لَهُ شِكْلاً﴾ يوافقه ويصلح له، فالمرأة للرجل، والأتان للحمار، والرمكة للفرس، وثياب الرجال للرجال لا تصلح للنساء، وثياب النساء لا تصلح للرجال، وكذلك ما شاكلها على هذا.

وروى علي بن أبي طلحة عنه قال: خلق الله سبحانه الخلق كلّهم بقدر، وخلق لهم الخير والشر، فخير الخير السعادة، وشر الشر الشقاوة.

﴿وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا الْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِنْ مُدَّكِرٍ﴾ ﴿كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِالنُّذُرِ﴾ ﴿فَقالُوا أَبَشَراً مِنَّا وَاحِداً نَتَّبِعُهُ إِنَّا إِذاً لَفِي ضَلالٍ وَسُعُرٍ﴾. "أبشراً آدميّا واحدا منّا نتبعه ونحن جماعة كثيرة وهو واحد": وقرأ أبو السماك العدوي بالرفع، وكلا الوجهين سائغ في عائد الذكر. ﴿إِنَّا إِذاً﴾: إن فعلنا ذلك وتركنا دين آبائنا وتابعناه على دينه، وهو واحد منا آدمي مثلنا. ﴿لَفِي ضَلالٍ﴾: ذهاب عن الصواب. ﴿وَسُعُرٍ﴾: قال ابن عباس: يعني وعذاب. وقال الحسن: شدة العذاب. وقال قتادة: عناء. وقال سفيان بن عيينة: هو جمع سعيرة. وقال الفراء: جنون، يقال: ناقة مسعورة إذا كانت خفيفة الرأس هائمة على وجهها. قال الشاعر يصف ناقة:

تخال بها سعرا إذا السفر هزها ... ذميل وإيقاع من السير متعب [تفسير القرطبي: 17/138.]

وقال وهب: ﴿وَسُعُرٍ﴾: أي بُعد من الحق.

﴿أَأُلْقِيَ الذِّكْرُ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ بَيْنِنَا﴾: أأُنزل الوحي عليه من بيننا؟ ﴿بَلْ هُوَ كَذَّابٌ أَشِرٌ﴾: بطِر، مرِح، متكبر، يريد أن يتعاظم علينا بادعائه النبوة.

وقال عبد الرحمن بن أبي حماد: الأشِر هو الذي لا يبالي ما قال. وقرأ مجاهد ﴿أَشُرٌ﴾ بفتح الألف وضم الشين، وهما لغتان مثل: حَذِر وحَذُر، ويَقِظ ويَقُظ، وعَجِل وعَجُل، ومَجِد ومَجُد الشجاع.

﴿سَيَعْلَمُونَ غَداً﴾: بالتاء قراءة الشامي، وقرأ الأعمش ويحيى وابن ثوبان وحمزة وغيرهم بالياء. فمن قرأ بالتاء فهو من قول صالح لهم، ومن قرأ بالياء فهو من قول الله سبحانه. ومعنى الكلام: في الغد القريب، على عادة الناس في قولهم للعواقب: إنّ مع اليوم غداً، وإنّ مع اليوم أخاه غداً، وأراد به وقت نزول العذاب بهم. ﴿مَنِ الْكَذَّابُ الْأَشِرُ﴾: قرأ أبو قلابة ﴿مَنِ الْكَذَّابُ الْأَشَرُّ﴾ بفتح الشين وتشديد الراء على وزن أفعل من الشر، والقراءة الصحيحة ما عليه العامة.

قال أبو حاتم: لا يكاد العربي يتكلم بالأشرّ والأخيّر إلا في ضرورة الشعر، كقول رؤبة:

بلال خير الناس وابن الأخير

إنما يقولون: خير وشر. قال الله عز وجل: ﴿كُنْتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ﴾، وقال سبحانه: ﴿أَنْتُمْ شَرٌّ مَكاناً﴾.

﴿إِنَّا مُرْسِلُوا النَّاقَةِ﴾: باعثوها ومخرجوها من الهضبة التي سألوا. ﴿فِتْنَةً لَهُمْ﴾: محنة. ﴿فَارْتَقِبْهُمْ﴾: وانتظرهم، ﴿وَاصْطَبِرْ﴾: واصبر على ظلمهم وأذاهم، ولا تعجل حتى يأتيهم أمري. ﴿وَاصْطَبِرْ﴾ افتعال من الصبر، وأصل الطاء فيه تاء، فحُوِّلت طاءً لأجل الصاد.

﴿وَنَبِّئْهُمْ أَنَّ الْمَاءَ قِسْمَةٌ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ وبين الناقة بالسوية: لها يوم ولهم يوم. وإنما قال: ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ لأن العرب إذا أخبرت عن بني آدم وعن البهائم غلّبوا بني آدم على البهائم. ﴿كُلُّ شِرْبٍ مُحْتَضَرٌ﴾: نصيب من الماء يحضره من كانت نوبته، فإذا كان يوم الناقة حضرت شربها، وإذا كان يومهم حضروا شربهم. وقال مجاهد: يعني يحضرون الماء إذا غابت الناقة، وإذا جاءت حضروا اللبن.

﴿فَنَادَوْا صاحِبَهُمْ فَتَعاطى فَعَقَرَ﴾: صاحبهم هو قدار بن سالف، وكان أشقر، ولذلك قيل له: أشقر ثمود. فتناول الناقة بسيفه فعقرها، ولذلك سمّت العرب الجزار "قداراً" تشبيهاً به. وقال الشاعر:

إنا لنضرب بالسيوف رؤوسهم ... ضرب القدار نقيعة القدام [تفسير القرطبي: 17/139.]

﴿فَكَيْفَ كانَ عَذابِي وَنُذُرِ﴾. ثم بيّن عذابهم فقال عز من قائل: ﴿إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ صَيْحَةً واحِدَةً فَكانُوا كَهَشِيمِ الْمُحْتَظِرِ﴾. قرأ الحسن وقتادة ﴿الْمُحْتَظَرِ﴾ بفتح الظاء، أراد الحظيرة، وقرأ الباقون بكسر الظاء، أرادوا صاحب الحظيرة.

قال ابن عباس: هو أن الرجل يجعل لغنمه حظيرة بالشجر والشوك دون السباع، فما سقط من ذلك فداسته الغنم فهو الهشيم. وقال قتادة: يعني كالعظام النخرة المحترقة، وهي رواية العوفي عن ابن عباس، ورواية أبي ظبيان عنه أيضاً. وقيل: كحشيش تأكله الغنم. وقال سعيد بن جبير: هو التراب الذي يتناثر من الحائط. وقال ابن زيد: هو الشجر البالي الذي تهشّم حتى ذرّته الريح، والعرب تسمي كل شيء كان رطباً فيبس هشيماً.

﴿وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا﴾ هوّنّا عليهم ﴿الْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِنْ مُدَّكِرٍ﴾. ﴿كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ لُوطٍ بِالنُّذُرِ﴾. ﴿إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ حاصِباً﴾: ريحاً ترميهم بالحَصْباء، وهي الحصى. وقال بعضهم: هو الحجر نفسه. قال الضحاك: يعني صغار الحصى. والحاصب والحَصْب والحَصْباء هي الحجر الذي دون ملء الكف، والمحصَّب الموضع الذي يُرمى فيه الجمار. وقال سعيد بن المسيب: سمعت عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه يقول لأهل المدينة: "حصّبوا المسجد"، أي صبّوا فيه الحجارة.

﴿ثم استثنى فقال: إِلَّا آلَ لُوطٍ﴾: أي أتباعه على دينه من أهله وأمته، ﴿نَجَّيْناهُمْ﴾ من العذاب ﴿بِسَحَرٍ﴾. قال الأخفش: إنما أجراه لأنه نكرة، ومجازه: بسحرٍ من الأسحار، ولو أراد سحر يوم بعينه لقال: "سَحَرَ" غير مجرى، ونظيره قوله: ﴿اهْبِطُوا مِصْراً﴾.

﴿نِعْمَةً﴾ يعني: كان ذلك، أو جعلناه ﴿نِعْمَةً مِنْ عِنْدِنا﴾ عليهم حيث أنجيناهم وأهلكنا أعداءهم. ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾ كما جزيناهم، لوطاً وآله، ﴿نَجْزِي مَنْ شَكَرَ﴾ فآمن بالله وأطاعه.

﴿وَلَقَدْ أَنْذَرَهُمْ لوط بَطْشَتَنا﴾ أي أخذنا لهم بالعقوبة قبل حلولها بهم. ﴿فَتَمارَوْا بِالنُّذُرِ﴾ فكذّبوا بإنذاره شكاً منهم فيه، وهو تفاعل من المِرية.

﴿وَلَقَدْ راوَدُوهُ عَنْ ضَيْفِهِ﴾: طالبوه وسألوه أن يُخلّي بينهم وبينهم. يقول العرب: راده يرُوده، وارتاده، وراوده يراوده، نظيرها. ﴿وَراوَدَتْهُ الَّتِي هُوَ فِي بَيْتِها عَنْ نَفْسِهِ﴾.

﴿فَطَمَسْنا أَعْيُنَهُمْ﴾ أي أعميناهم، وصيّرناها كسائر الوجه لا يُرى لها شق. وذلك أنهم لما قصدوا دار لوط عليه السلام وعالجوا بابه ليدخلوا، قالت الرسل للوط: خلِّ بينهم وبين الدخول، ﴿فَإِنَّا رُسُلُ رَبِّكَ لَنْ يَصِلُوا إِلَيْكَ﴾. فدخلوا الدار، فاستأذن جبريل ربَّه عز وجل في عقوبتهم فأذن له، فصفقهم بجناحه، فتركهم عمياً يترددون متحيرين لا يهتدون إلى الباب، وأخرجهم لوط عمياً لا يبصرون. هذا قول عامة المفسرين. وقال الضحاك: طمس الله على أبصارهم، فلم يروا الرسل، وقالوا: قد رأيناهم حين دخلوا البيت، فأين ذهبوا؟ فلم يروهم، ورجعوا. ﴿فَذُوقُوا عَذابِي وَنُذُرِ﴾.

﴿وَلَقَدْ صَبَّحَهُمْ﴾ جاءهم العذاب وقت الصبح ﴿بُكْرَةً عَذابٌ مُسْتَقِرٌّ﴾ دائم عام، استقر فيهم حتى يُقضى بهم إلى عذاب الآخرة.

﴿فَذُوقُوا عَذابِي وَنُذُرِ﴾. ﴿وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا الْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِنْ مُدَّكِرٍ﴾. ﴿وَلَقَدْ جاءَ آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ النُّذُرُ﴾ يعني موسى وهارون عليهما السلام. ﴿كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا التسع كُلِّها فَأَخَذْناهُمْ بالعذاب أَخْذَ عَزِيزٍ مُقْتَدِرٍ﴾: قادر لا يعجزه ما أراد.

ثم خوّف أهل مكة فقال عز من قائل: ﴿أَكُفَّارُكُمْ خَيْرٌ مِنْ أُولئِكُمْ﴾ الذين أحللت بهم نقمتي: من قوم نوح، وعاد، وثمود، وقوم لوط، وآل فرعون؟ ﴿أَمْ لَكُمْ بَراءَةٌ﴾ من العذاب ﴿فِي الزُّبُرِ﴾: الكتب، تأمنون بها؟

﴿أَمْ يَقُولُونَ﴾ يعني كفار مكة: ﴿نَحْنُ جَمِيعٌ مُنْتَصِرٌ﴾ أي جماعة لا تُرام ولا تُضام، ولا يقصدنا أحد بسوء، ولا يريد حربنا وتفريق جمعنا إلا انتقمنا منه. وكان حقه: "منتصرون"، فتبع رؤوس الآي.

﴿سَيُهْزَمُ الْجَمْعُ﴾: قراءة العامة على غير تسمية الفاعل، وقرأ يعقوب بالنون والنصب وكسر الزاي وفتح العين على التعظيم. ﴿وَيُوَلُّونَ الدُّبُرَ﴾ أي الأدبار، فوحّد والمراد الجمع لأجل رؤوس الآي، كما يقال: ضربنا منهم الرؤوس، وضربنا منهم الرأس، إذا كان الواحد يؤدي عن معنى جميعه. فصدق الله سبحانه وتعالى وعده، وهزمهم يوم بدر.

قال مقاتل: ضرب أبو جهل فرسه فتقدم يوم بدر في الصف وقال: "نحن منتصرون اليوم من محمد وأصحابه".

قال سعيد بن المسيب: سمعت عمر بن الخطاب لما نزلت ﴿سَيُهْزَمُ الْجَمْعُ وَيُوَلُّونَ الدُّبُرَ﴾ قال: كنت لا أدري أي جمع نُهزم؟ فلما كان يوم بدر رأيت النبي ﷺ ثبت في درعه ويقول: ﴿سَيُهْزَمُ الْجَمْعُ وَيُوَلُّونَ الدُّبُرَ﴾.

﴿بَلِ السَّاعَةُ مَوْعِدُهُمْ﴾ جميعاً، ﴿وَالسَّاعَةُ أَدْهى وَأَمَرُّ﴾: أعظم بليّةً وأشد مرارةً من عذاب يوم بدر.

أخبرني الحسين بن محمد قال: حدّثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: حدّثنا محمد بن إبراهيم بن زياد قال: حدّثنا أبو مصعب قال: حدّثنا مجرد بن هارون، عن الأعرج، عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: «بادروا بالأعمال سبعاً: ما ينتظرون إلا فقراً منسياً، أو غنىً مطغياً [الصحاح: 3/1293.]، أو مرضاً مفسداً، أو هرماً مفنداً، أو موتاً مجهزاً، والدجال شر غائب يُنتظر، والساعة أدهى وأمر».

[156]

﴿إِنَّ الْمُجْرِمِينَ فِي ضَلالٍ وَسُعُرٍ﴾: قال الضحاك: يعني ناراً ستُعرض عليهم.

قال الحسين بن الفضل: ﴿إِنَّ الْمُجْرِمِينَ فِي ضَلالٍ﴾ في الدنيا، ﴿وَسُعُرٍ﴾ نارٍ في الآخرة. وقال ابن كيسان: بُعدٍ من الحق. وقيل: جنون. وقال قتادة: في عناء وعذاب. ثم بيّن عذابهم فقال: ﴿يَوْمَ يُسْحَبُونَ فِي النَّارِ عَلى وُجُوهِهِمْ﴾ يُجرّون، ويقال لهم: ﴿ذُوقُوا مَسَّ سَقَرَ﴾، وإنما هو كقولك: "ذق المرَّ، السياطَ".

﴿إِنَّا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ﴾ بالنصب قراءة العامة، وقرأ أبو السماك العدوي بالرفع ﴿خَلَقْناهُ بِقَدَرٍ﴾. قال الحسن: قدّر الله لكل شيء من خلقه قدرَه الذي ينبغي له. وقال الربيع: هو كقوله: ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدْراً﴾، أي أجلاً لا يتقدم ولا يتأخر. وقال ابن عباس: ﴿إِنَّا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ جَعَلْنا لَهُ شِكْلاً﴾ يوافقه ويصلح له، فالمرأة للرجل، والأتان للحمار، والرمكة للفرس، وثياب الرجال للرجال لا تصلح للنساء، وثياب النساء لا تصلح للرجال، وكذلك ما شاكلها على هذا.

وروى علي بن أبي طلحة عنه قال: خلق الله سبحانه الخلق كلّهم بقدر، وخلق لهم الخير والشر، فخير الخير السعادة، وشر الشر الشقاوة.

﴿وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا الْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِنْ مُدَّكِرٍ﴾ ﴿كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِالنُّذُرِ﴾ ﴿فَقالُوا أَبَشَراً مِنَّا وَاحِداً نَتَّبِعُهُ إِنَّا إِذاً لَفِي ضَلالٍ وَسُعُرٍ﴾. "أبشراً آدميّا واحدا منّا نتبعه ونحن جماعة كثيرة وهو واحد": وقرأ أبو السماك العدوي بالرفع، وكلا الوجهين سائغ في عائد الذكر. ﴿إِنَّا إِذاً﴾: إن فعلنا ذلك وتركنا دين آبائنا وتابعناه على دينه، وهو واحد منا آدمي مثلنا. ﴿لَفِي ضَلالٍ﴾: ذهاب عن الصواب. ﴿وَسُعُرٍ﴾: قال ابن عباس: يعني وعذاب. وقال الحسن: شدة العذاب. وقال قتادة: عناء. وقال سفيان بن عيينة: هو جمع سعيرة. وقال الفراء: جنون، يقال: ناقة مسعورة إذا كانت خفيفة الرأس هائمة على وجهها. قال الشاعر يصف ناقة:

تخال بها سعرا إذا السفر هزها ... ذميل وإيقاع من السير متعب [تفسير القرطبي: 17/138.]

وقال وهب: ﴿وَسُعُرٍ﴾: أي بُعد من الحق.

﴿أَأُلْقِيَ الذِّكْرُ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ بَيْنِنَا﴾: أأُنزل الوحي عليه من بيننا؟ ﴿بَلْ هُوَ كَذَّابٌ أَشِرٌ﴾: بطِر، مرِح، متكبر، يريد أن يتعاظم علينا بادعائه النبوة.

وقال عبد الرحمن بن أبي حماد: الأشِر هو الذي لا يبالي ما قال. وقرأ مجاهد ﴿أَشُرٌ﴾ بفتح الألف وضم الشين، وهما لغتان مثل: حَذِر وحَذُر، ويَقِظ ويَقُظ، وعَجِل وعَجُل، ومَجِد ومَجُد الشجاع.

﴿سَيَعْلَمُونَ غَداً﴾: بالتاء قراءة الشامي، وقرأ الأعمش ويحيى وابن ثوبان وحمزة وغيرهم بالياء. فمن قرأ بالتاء فهو من قول صالح لهم، ومن قرأ بالياء فهو من قول الله سبحانه. ومعنى الكلام: في الغد القريب، على عادة الناس في قولهم للعواقب: إنّ مع اليوم غداً، وإنّ مع اليوم أخاه غداً، وأراد به وقت نزول العذاب بهم. ﴿مَنِ الْكَذَّابُ الْأَشِرُ﴾: قرأ أبو قلابة ﴿مَنِ الْكَذَّابُ الْأَشَرُّ﴾ بفتح الشين وتشديد الراء على وزن أفعل من الشر، والقراءة الصحيحة ما عليه العامة.

قال أبو حاتم: لا يكاد العربي يتكلم بالأشرّ والأخيّر إلا في ضرورة الشعر، كقول رؤبة:
